headline: Futures rally on trade-summit hopes even as retail sentiment sours
body: Equity futures are pointing to a firmly higher open Monday, with S&P 500 contracts up roughly 0.6%-0.7%, Nasdaq-100 futures gaining about 1%, and Dow futures adding more than 400 points. The lift follows a rough stretch: stocks absorbed a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike on September 16 that pushed the target range to 3.75%-4.00%, then closed out the week lower as a $1 trillion-plus triple-witching options expiration collided with a Bank of Japan decision and the 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5%. Today's bounce looks driven less by domestic data than by geopolitics and energy: crude oil is sliding for a fourth straight session on hopes for a US-Iran diplomatic thaw and restored Saudi pipeline capacity, while investors look ahead to Thursday's Trump-Xi summit, expected to address the tariff truce and AI cooperation.

Positioning data tells a more cautious story than the tape. The latest AAII survey showed bearish sentiment jumping to 53.3% versus just 28.8% bullish, the weakest retail-optimism reading since May 2025, as the rate hike and elevated oil and yields weighed on mood. That gap — futures rallying while the AAII gauge sits near multi-month lows — suggests today's move is being led by summit headlines and falling crude rather than a broad shift in retail conviction. Beyond the survey, chatter on Reddit and StockTwits skewed toward scattered speculative names rather than any clear directional call on the broader market, so this read leans more on price action and macro catalysts than on social sentiment.
